# Find Funding

Finding funding happens at the school/college/unit level by the research project team and the principal investigator (PI). This page helps point you to the various U-M resources that help project teams find funding.

## How can ORSP help in this early phase of the Research Project Lifecycle?

ORSP does _not_ handle research development nor finding funding, but we _can_ point you in the right direction.
In the early stages of a research project lifecycle, ORSP reminds project teams to:

* In your proposal development, plan ahead for compliance with ORSP's [proposal submission deadline policy](https://orsp.umich.edu/route-submit-proposal/proposal-submission-deadline-policy) .
* Utilize ORSP for **negotiation and review of agreements and grants .**
* Remember **that ORSP has signature authority** assigned by the university.
* At the University of Michigan, _all_ sponsored projects must be submitted through ORSP via the eResearch Proposal Management (eRPM) system.

# Brian Gilchrist

## Chief Pediatric Surgery in Brooklyn, NY

[View my portfolio](http://www.brian-gilchrist.com)

Dr. Brian Gilchrist is a respected presence in the New York medical community who guides NYU-Winthrop University and held responsibilities as chief of pediatric surgery there until early 2019. Successful in building and expanding a dynamic program, Dr. Brian Gilchrist worked to ensure that the pediatric surgery trauma system functioned at the highest possible level.

From 2014 to 2018, Dr. Gilchrist served as chairman of surgery at the Bronx-Lebanon Hospital Center, and also guided the residency program for general surgery. Ensuring a high quality of care and sustained academic learning, he was selected staff surgeon of the year by surgical residents in 2015, and the following year earned teacher of the year recognition from New York Medical College students.
During this time, one of his responsibilities was overseeing the hospital’s morbidity and mortality conferences.

Over the years, Dr. Gilchrist has published more than 80 peer-reviewed articles, while also lecturing in his field at venues worldwide. Speaking before the New England Surgical Society in Maine in 2012, Dr. Brian Gilchrist gave a presentation titled “Argon Beam Coagulation Negates the Need for Drainage in the Excision of Cystic Hygromas."

# Brian Cleary Awarded $2.25M NIH Grant to Advance Single-Cell Gene Expression Research

Boston University’s [Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences](https://www.bu.edu/cds-faculty/) (CDS) is proud to announce that [Brian Cleary](https://www.bu.edu/cds-faculty/profile/bcleary/) , Assistant Professor of Computing & Data Sciences, Biology, and Biomedical Engineering, has secured a $2.25 million grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to support his groundbreaking research in computational biology. Cleary is the sole principal investigator (PI) on the five-year project, “ _Measuring and modeling gene expression trajectories: new computational-experimental approaches_ .”

Headshot of Brian Cleary, BU Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences Brian Cleary, Assistant Professor, BU Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences
The research aims to deepen understanding of how gene expression changes over time within single cells—an area central to development, tissue function, and disease progression. Cleary’s approach combines new computationally informed experimental strategies, methods to track RNA across multiple timepoints, and tools to model RNA velocity vector fields. The result will be a more systematic, quantitative understanding of how cell physiology influences “total RNA velocity.”

The project will be housed in Cleary’s [Algorithmic Lens on Biology Lab](https://www.algobiolab.com/) , part of CDS’s growing AI for Science initiative. By uniting computation with experimental design, the lab seeks to build tools that advance both fundamental biology and biomedical applications.
